A queued wake is not proof that an agent started. In EI-25449656496811250, the release reviewer finished its previous turn at 21:26Z. A carry-respawn process remained alive, but no new native transcript appeared and required wakes repeatedly parked as pending-delivery-id.

## The measured cause

The managed host's codex-starting-stuck-snapshot showed the Codex startup Update available dialog (0.161.0 to 0.162.0). Its options required a human action before normal startup. The host correctly refused to attest a native session: respawn-binding-unconfirmed, reason successor-native-id-missing. Neither a live PID nor queued wake proved pickup.

Read the exact owner's host metadata and bounded lifecycle snapshot, revalidate process birth identity, and check the newest native transcript. Do not diagnose quota, overload or resource exhaustion from these symptoms. Do not resume a live source through capability:launch-agent: it auto-forks and would create a second reviewer.

## Immediate recovery and durable guard

For this incident, the existing interruptViaPty(owner, 'esc') helper sent Escape to the identity-checked update modal. It skipped the optional update, without killing, forking or upgrading. At21:57:38Z the host bound native01a11d85, then delivered a turn; the actual reviewer reply approved preparation at22:00Z. Transport acceptance alone was not treated as success.

The maintained codexManagedFeaturesToml composition now emits check_for_update_on_startup=false before the first TOML table. It covers interactive role/SU and spawned Codex homes. ensureSuCodexHomeConfig includes the parsed setting in readiness, so older missing/true configurations are repaired without deleting native history. Preserve account routing and credentials when repairing an existing home.

OpenAI's Configuration Reference documents this boolean and recommends false only when updates are centrally managed: https://developers.openai.com/codex/config-reference . Managed agent launches use the workspace's CLI installation rather than choosing an update from a child startup dialog.

## Recurrence evidence

The new registered role-home test was red before the change because the parsed property was undefined. The complete role-home and shared configuration suites passed81 tests with zero failures/skips (test-run rows20939106 and20939109). They cover generated role/SU settings, resume repair retaining transcript bytes, and the shared spawned-home composition's top-level ordering. A startup guard does not imply the unrelated release candidate is accepted; its source/producer/physical/GO gates remain separate.
